headline: High risk of prompt-injection and data leakage if Claude Code ingests repo content from the unverified prompt-engineering corpus.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Profile A is a content-writing repository with prompt-engineering material, while Profile B reads files, uses MCP, and processes stdin/stdout. That creates a plausible bridge where A’s content can be fed into B as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Profile A content is copied into a file or MCP payload that Profile B reads as instructions
IF Profile B is configured to treat repository text as authoritative prompts
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate directories
Disable MCP servers that ingest untrusted text
Add a manual review step before B executes instructions from A
Use a prompt-injection filter on any A-derived content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all A-to-B text flows

B_data_leakage.rationale: Profile B can read and write files in the working directory and handles git history and shell environment; Profile A is a repository of prompt-engineering content. If A and B share a workspace, B can expose or transform A’s files, and B’s docs show broad file access. The pairwise leakage pathway is plausible in default terminal workflows.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same working tree
IF A contains sensitive notes or prompts in files that B can read
mitigations: Place A and B in separate workspaces
Restrict B to a read-only mount for A’s files
Remove secrets from the shared directory
Review git diffs before commit
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Profile B has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, with shared state via filesystem and git. Profile A is a repository artifact that can be edited or regenerated. Concurrent edits can collide on the same files or git state; the profile explicitly says shared state exists via filesystem and git only, so conflict is credible.
conditions: IF A and B write to the same repository or branch
IF B runs multiple instances against the same git checkout
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Serialize writes with a lock file
Have B commit only after manual review
Run one agent at a time on the shared repo
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Profile A is a prompt-engineering corpus that may produce guidance or examples, and Profile B can act on file and shell outputs. If B treats A’s text as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes or shell actions. There is no documented verification barrier between them, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated instructions without independent verification
IF A’s output is used to drive shell commands or file edits
mitigations: Require B to cite sources before acting
Add a human approval step for shell commands
Compare A’s claims against a second source
Limit B to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: implement output validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Profile B handles git credentials and shell environment, while Profile A is a public open-source repository with no declared regulated data classes. I do not see a direct residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles, so only a low compliance concern remains, mainly around accidental secret handling in B.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into the shared workspace
IF B’s environment contains secrets that are copied into A-derived artifacts
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the repo
Rotate any exposed credentials
Use separate accounts for repo work and secret-bearing sessions
Review logs before sharing
requires-engineering: add secret-scanning and retention controls
